title: The same supplier, excused from competition year after year
question: Which suppliers were given a new contract without competitive bidding in four or more different fiscal years?
finding: 983 suppliers hold at least one contract awarded without competition since July 2018. 56 of them were given a new one in four or more different fiscal years, and 4 in at least eight of the nine. The longest runs: Five Keys Schools And Programs (9 years, 20 contracts, $224.2 million); One Treasure Island (9 years, 10 contracts, $19.2 million); Rubicon Enterprises Inc (9 years, 9 contracts, $16.6 million); Toolworks Inc (9 years, 9 contracts, $2.9 million).
how: Contracts in the Supplier Contracts table that started on or after 1 July 2018 under an emergency, sole-source, ordinance-waiver or other "not bid" rule, grouped by the prime contractor’s name. A year counts when at least one such contract started in it. Other public bodies are left out. "Paid" is payments to the supplier under those rules in the payment file.
limits: Each of these routes is written into the Administrative Code with a stated condition: a real emergency, a real single source, a class of work the Board has excused from bidding. A maker of proprietary software or hospital equipment is the only possible source every year, and a homelessness provider is covered by the Board’s standing waiver every year. A long run shows that the market has not been tested for that work in that time; it does not show that the supplier would have lost a competition. Names are grouped as written, so one supplier keyed two ways is undercounted. The paid figures count payments issued in fiscal 2019 or later, which is read from the voucher number and not from the year the file lists a line under; $1.08 billion that the whole payment file lists under those years was issued earlier and is left out.
